entities.summary: Nathan Abshire was an American Cajun accordion player. His time in the U.S. Army inspired Abshire to write the crooner song "Service Blues", which the newspaper Daily World reported as "one of his most memorable tearjerkers". After the war, he settled in Basile, Louisiana, where he played regularly at the Avalon Club. He released his best-known record, "Pine Grove Blues", in 1949. Abshire's music became more well known outside of Louisiana at the 1964 Newport Folk Festival. Abshire was never able to write so he was unable to sign autographs, resulting in him having to politely decline the requests.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Nathan Abshire's accordion playing and songwriting had a significant regional impact in Louisiana, contributing to the preservation of Cajun culture. His music also gained popularity outside of Louisiana through performances at the Newport Folk Festival.
